title: Sustained Windows Context-Switch Rate Deviation
exclusions: Reports a host only when three consecutive five-minute averages of native `System\Context Switches/sec` each exceed both twice that host's trailing baseline mean and the mean plus three standard deviations. Microsoft defines the counter as the system-wide rate at which processors switch thread context. A result does not prove contention, excessive threads, driver defect, interrupt storm, CPU saturation, application regression, or service impact; context switches also occur normally for scheduling and waits. It excludes process/thread attribution, hosts with fewer than 144 prior five-minute baseline points, zero/invalid values, gaps, and other processor counters. The 24-hour/144-point baseline, 2x and 3-sigma gates, 15-minute persistence, 60-second collection and five-minute close delay are local starting policies, not Microsoft or Splunk thresholds. Workload seasonality, CPU-count/VM changes, clock skew, duplicate inputs and delayed samples can distort the baseline and belong in source/configuration health. This UC does not tune threads, priorities, CPU, VM allocation, drivers or services.
evidence: Retain the version-controlled `windows_context_switch_rate_deviation` search, cron, ACL and results; every row with host, three bucket times/rates, baseline sample count/mean/deviation, ratio and sigma thresholds, source metadata and index time; raw Perfmon samples; exact inputs.conf/deployment version and English-name setting; expected-host, interval, delay, duplicates and configuration-change health; CPU/logical-processor/VM inventory; correlated Processor Queue Length, CPU user/privileged/interrupt/DPC, System Calls, process thread/context and service SLO data; incident/change/baseline approvals, alert delivery, disposition and dated positive, negative, gap, flat-baseline, seasonality, resize and upgrade tests. This documentation review sampled no counter, dispatched no SPL and changed no runtime system.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Under absolute test bounds, provide at least 144 valid five-minute buckets for host `cpu-lab-01` with trailing baseline mean 1000 context switches/sec and standard deviation 100, followed by three gap-free buckets at 2200, 2300 and 2400. Expect one row at the third bucket with `recent_anomaly_points=3`, span 600 seconds, ratio threshold 2000, sigma threshold 1300, and latest rate 2400.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows independently for: only two anomalous buckets; 1900/2200/2300 where one fails 2x; three anomalies separated by a missing five-minute bucket; fewer than 144 baseline points; baseline mean zero; nonnumeric/negative Value; wrong object/counter/source/source type; stale or newest excluded samples; and duplicate raw samples identified by health. Test a VM CPU resize and workload schedule change: baseline must be reset/retrained under an approved policy rather than treated as a confirmed defect.

dataSources: Native Windows performance counter `\System\Context Switches/sec`, a system-wide rate across all processors. Configure a 60-second Splunk perfmon input with Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) to deployment-choice `index=perfmon`, exact supported `sourcetype=Perfmon:System`. Required fields: `_time, _indextime, host, object, counter, Value, source, sourcetype`; preserve instance if emitted. Correlate `System\Processor Queue Length`, `System\System Calls/sec`, `Processor Information(_Total)\% Processor Time`, `% Privileged Time`, `% Interrupt Time`, `% DPC Time`, Interrupts/sec, Process Thread Count and service-response metrics. Use `useEnglishOnly=true` and validate names.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) and the Splunk Windows perfmon input. A local operations app owns the analytic, baseline/configuration health, fixtures, dashboard and `windows_context_switch_exceptions.csv`.
spl:
index=perfmon sourcetype="Perfmon:System" object="System" counter="Context Switches/sec" earliest=-25h latest=-5m@m
| eval destination=lower(trim(host)), context_switches_per_sec=tonumber(Value)
| where len(destination)>0 AND isnotnull(context_switches_per_sec) AND context_switches_per_sec>=0
| bin _time span=5m
| stats avg(context_switches_per_sec) AS context_switches_per_sec count AS raw_sample_count max(_indextime) AS last_indextime values(source) AS observed_sources values(sourcetype) AS observed_sourcetypes by destination _time
| sort 0 destination _time
| streamstats window=288 current=false count AS baseline_samples avg(context_switches_per_sec) AS baseline_avg stdev(context_switches_per_sec) AS baseline_stdev by destination
| eval baseline_stdev=coalesce(baseline_stdev,0), ratio_threshold=baseline_avg*2, sigma_threshold=baseline_avg+(3*baseline_stdev), is_anomaly=if(baseline_samples>=144 AND baseline_avg>0 AND context_switches_per_sec>ratio_threshold AND context_switches_per_sec>sigma_threshold,1,0)
| streamstats window=3 current=true count AS recent_point_count sum(is_anomaly) AS recent_anomaly_points earliest(_time) AS first_anomaly_bucket latest(_time) AS latest_anomaly_bucket by destination
| eventstats max(_time) AS newest_host_bucket by destination
| where _time=newest_host_bucket AND _time>=relative_time(now(),"-20m@m") AND recent_point_count=3 AND recent_anomaly_points=3 AND latest_anomaly_bucket-first_anomaly_bucket=600
| eval latest_context_switches_per_sec=round(context_switches_per_sec,2), baseline_avg=round(baseline_avg,2), baseline_stdev=round(baseline_stdev,2), ratio_threshold=round(ratio_threshold,2), sigma_threshold=round(sigma_threshold,2), baseline_window_hours=24, minimum_baseline_points=144, bucket_minutes=5, required_consecutive_buckets=3, close_delay_minutes=5, analytic_interpretation="sustained host-relative context-switch-rate deviation; correlate CPU, queue, interrupt/DPC, threads and service impact; not root-cause proof", use_case="UC-1.2.70"
| table destination first_anomaly_bucket latest_anomaly_bucket recent_point_count recent_anomaly_points latest_context_switches_per_sec baseline_samples baseline_avg baseline_stdev ratio_threshold sigma_threshold raw_sample_count observed_sources observed_sourcetypes last_indextime baseline_window_hours minimum_baseline_points bucket_minutes required_consecutive_buckets close_delay_minutes analytic_interpretation use_case
| sort 0 -latest_context_switches_per_sec destination
description: Reports the latest host row when three gap-free five-minute `System\Context Switches/sec` averages all exceed host-relative 2x-mean and 3-sigma gates derived from prior samples. It reports the current rate and baseline evidence at host/system grain; additional counters and service telemetry are required for cause and impact.
value: A sustained deviation in system-wide context switching can expose workload, scheduling or kernel-path changes early enough to compare releases, VM sizing and service latency before degradation becomes chronic. A host-relative dual threshold avoids unsupported universal rates and provides reproducible evidence for targeted performance analysis.
implementation: Collect `System\Context Switches/sec` every 60 seconds with English counter names and validate a complete, unique host series. Save `windows_context_switch_rate_deviation`, schedule every five minutes, and alert only after the three-bucket dual-threshold condition. Route with asset/service and recent CPU/VM/change context; use queue, CPU mode, DPC/interrupt, thread/process and response-time telemetry plus WPA/WPR or vendor diagnostics before remediation.
visualization: Operations dashboard `Windows — Context-Switch Rate Deviation`: source cadence/delay/duplicate and baseline-readiness health first; five-minute rate with baseline, 2x and 3-sigma lines; anomalies by host/service; correlated queue, CPU user/privileged/interrupt/DPC, interrupts, system calls and thread counts; VM/CPU changes; table matching SPL output; exceptions and outcomes. Label “system-wide anomaly—not process attribution or root cause.”
schema: Windows System performance object, Context Switches/sec counter
dataModelAcceleration: The CIM Performance CPU dataset does not define an exact system-wide context-switch-rate field with the host-relative baseline and continuity semantics used here. CPU load is only correlation and cannot replace the counter. No `cimSpl` is claimed; metrics-index or summary optimization must preserve host, rate, five-minute buckets, baseline exclusion and raw parity.

knownFalsePositives:
A result is a real host-relative rate deviation; benign or expected explanations include:

1. **Planned load test, batch, compilation, backup or analytics window** — high thread activity can legitimately change scheduling. Match exact job/run, process/thread counts, throughput, response SLO, host set and UTC bounds.
2. **Application deployment, runtime upgrade or thread-pool change** — a release can alter thread count, locking, I/O waits or request concurrency. Correlate deployment ID, process versions, before/after rates, latency/errors and rollback outcome.
3. **VM vCPU resize, migration or host contention** — topology/scheduling changes invalidate a prior baseline. Verify hypervisor event, vCPU/logical processor count, steal/ready equivalents, migration time and retraining approval.
4. **Security scan, EDR update or diagnostic profiler** — endpoint tools can add threads, kernel transitions and sampling overhead. Confirm product console job/update, process/driver version, destination scope and completion.
5. **Failover, restart, cache warm-up or traffic shift** — recovery changes concurrency and I/O patterns. Match orchestration/change, node role, traffic volume, queue/latency and return to baseline.
6. **Interrupt/DPC or driver activity without user-mode contention** — a real anomaly can stem from network/storage hardware or drivers. Correlate `% Interrupt Time`, `% DPC Time`, Interrupts/sec, device/driver events and WPA traces before assigning application cause.
7. **Duplicate/gapped perfmon collection or clock skew** — overlapping stanzas and irregular samples can distort averages/baselines. Repair interval, time synchronization and source ownership; source health is never an alert exception.
8. **Authorized performance experiment** — preserve result and outcome as evidence; suppress duplicate paging only for approved hosts and bounds.

**Safe suppression:** apply lookup windows_context_switch_exceptions.csv after base detection. Require exact `destination`, optional exact service/change constraint, exception ID, numeric inclusive `valid_from_epoch`, exclusive `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, ticket, expected rate envelope and baseline-reset decision. Reject wildcard fleet or open-ended entries. Preserve base results and never suppress source, duplicate, gap or baseline-readiness health.

detailedImplementation:
## Define the performance contract

Assign Windows performance, application/service, virtualization, hardware/driver, Splunk collection/content and on-call owners. Inventory each host's canonical name, service, environment, OS/build, physical/virtual placement, logical processor/vCPU count, workload schedule/timezone, maintenance windows, SLO and forwarding route. Restrict process/thread drilldowns through an operations Splunk role.

Microsoft defines `System\Context Switches/sec` as the system-wide rate at which processors switch from one thread to another. Context switching is normal: higher-priority readiness, waits and sharing among threads all contribute. There is no universal per-core threshold in the cited primary documentation. The local policy uses each host's trailing behavior and requires both 2x mean and 3 standard deviations for three consecutive five-minute buckets.

## Collect a stable System counter

Deploy Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows from Splunkbase 742. Manage this deployment-app `inputs.conf` contract:

```ini
[perfmon://System]
object = System
counters = Context Switches/sec;Processor Queue Length;System Calls/sec
instances = *
interval = 60
mode = single
useEnglishOnly = true
index = perfmon
disabled = 0
```

Validate `index=perfmon`, `sourcetype=Perfmon:System`, object, counter, numeric Value, host and 60-second cadence. Index is local policy. The System object has a system-wide context-switch rate; do not divide by core and call that a Microsoft threshold. Collect Processor Information/Process counters in their correct objects and source types.

```spl
index=perfmon sourcetype="Perfmon:System" object="System" counter="Context Switches/sec" earliest=-30m
| table _time _indextime host object counter instance Value source sourcetype
| sort 0 host _time
```

Compare with **Performance Monitor > System > Context Switches/sec** on representative hosts. Validate physical/VM, high/low core count, idle/busy and reboot cases. Record CPU topology and workload changes because they can invalidate historical comparability.

## Monitor source and baseline health

Create expected-host health for absent/stale samples, cadence outside 50–90 seconds, excessive `_indextime-_time`, duplicate host/counter/time from overlapping stanzas, nonnumeric/negative values, unknown hosts, clock skew, counter localization, disabled inputs and forwarder backlog. Baseline readiness requires at least 144 prior five-minute points; expose the actual sample count.

Track OS/runtime/driver changes, vCPU resize/migration, service placement and workload schedule. Define when to reset/retrain a baseline; never silently compare pre-resize and post-resize behavior. A 24-hour window may not represent weekly seasonality, so high-seasonality services need a longer parity-tested baseline design.

## Schedule and understand the dual-threshold SPL

Save as `windows_context_switch_rate_deviation`, schedule with cron `*/5 * * * *`, and trigger when result count exceeds zero. Search through `latest=-5m@m` to allow delivery; schedule on five-minute boundaries so the final bucket is closed. Measure p99 ingestion delay.

The query bins valid raw samples into five-minute averages. Ordered `streamstats window=288 current=false` computes baseline statistics from prior points and excludes the point being tested. At least 144 points and positive mean are required. A point is anomalous only above both mean-times-two and mean-plus-three-standard-deviations. A second three-point window requires all three anomalies and exactly 600 seconds between first and last; the newest-host filter prevents historical anomalies from paging now.

One result is a sustained host/system-rate deviation. It has no process attribution. The raw sample count helps expose overlapping data but source health remains authoritative. No CIM CPU-load substitute is equivalent.

At large scale, a 25-hour raw scan every five minutes can be costly. Build a five-minute summary or metrics series only after it reproduces host/time/rate, current-excluded baseline, sample count, dual thresholds, continuity and delayed-window results exactly.

## Validate and tune

Replay 144+ baseline buckets and the documented 2200/2300/2400 positive series under absolute bounds. Assert means, deviations, thresholds, points and span. Run negatives independently: two points, one ratio failure, gap, too few baseline points, zero baseline, invalid value, wrong source/counter, stale/latest delay and duplicates. Test flat baseline, outliers, DST/workload schedule, restart, vCPU resize, host rename and earliest/latest boundaries.

Generate a safe lab load with an approved thread/concurrency harness and compare Perfmon to Splunk. Correlate queue, user/privileged/interrupt/DPC CPU, interrupts, system calls, process thread counts and service latency. Use Windows Performance Recorder/Analyzer only under a performance-engineering plan; tracing can add overhead. Synthetic fixtures validate SPL, while lab tests validate collection—not production tuning.

Measure search runtime, scanned events, dashboard ACL/drilldowns, alert delivery/throttle, ticket routing and exception expiry. Tune per service after representative weekdays/weekends and peak periods. Record every threshold or baseline-window change.

## Investigate before remediation

Alert title: `Sustained context-switch-rate deviation on <destination>: <latest_context_switches_per_sec>/sec`. Analysts verify raw samples, cadence, duplicate status, baseline count and recent host/config changes. Compare workload/throughput and service SLO, Processor Queue Length, CPU modes, DPC/interrupt metrics, System Calls/sec, process thread/context data, I/O waits, locks/contention, GC/runtime behavior and hypervisor scheduling.

If kernel/interrupt correlation dominates, engage driver/hardware/network/storage owners and capture approved WPA/WPR/vendor diagnostics. If one process/thread pool and service degradation align, engage application owners with release/config evidence. A high rate with healthy throughput/latency may be an expected workload shift requiring retraining, not remediation.

Never automatically kill a process, change thread priorities, disable a driver, resize vCPU or restart a service from this result. Apply lookup windows_context_switch_exceptions.csv after base detection and preserve all source/baseline health. Review exceptions and outcomes after every OS, runtime, driver, VM or workload change.

## Troubleshoot

- No data: verify English object/counter names, stanza deployment, forwarder permissions/health, source type and index ACL.
- Baseline never ready: repair gaps/cadence or extend history; do not lower the minimum without documented statistical impact.
- One host dominates: verify duplicate inputs, CPU topology/workload and source timestamp before tuning.
- High switch rate but low CPU: possible waits/thread sharing; inspect throughput, queue, threads, I/O and locks rather than assuming no impact.
- High interrupt/DPC: investigate devices/drivers with approved traces; do not blame the application.
- Anomaly after vCPU resize: reset/retrain according to policy and preserve the change marker.
- CIM CPU view differs: expected; CPU load is correlated, not context-switch parity.
grandmaExplanation: We learn each Windows computer's normal rate of switching between threads and flag a large increase that lasts about fifteen minutes. Specialists still compare CPU, drivers, programs and service speed before deciding what caused it.
hardware: Windows hosts exposing the System performance object through a validated 60-second perfmon input. Non-Windows context-switch metrics, process-only counters, hosts with less than 12 hours of baseline data and systems collected under another schema require separate analytics.
